blind_spots.blind_spot: A 2-person company is simultaneously running a multi-year Navy in-situ-monitoring sensor-fusion program, an Army SBIR Phase II, and carrying forward prior Navy/Air Force-funded capability work, with no visible headcount growth.
blind_spots.operator_reality: When funded periods of performance end and only 2 people carry the technical, program-management, and reporting burden across three simultaneous service-branch efforts, sustainment of any single deliverable — like keeping the ML model current as new machines/materials are added — is the first thing to slip.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's public news reads as a steady string of technical wins (new funding, conference talks) without any corresponding story about scaling the team to match the workload.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Senvol has received funding from the U.S. Navy to lead a project focused on demonstrating that based on in-situ monitoring data...

blind_spots.blind_spot: The Senvol API is marketed for licensing into third-party software used by DLA and USAF for materials/parts research, with no mention of ITAR/export-control handling for the underlying AM machine and material process-parameter data.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Raw process-parameter data behind DoD parts qualification is exactly the kind of technical data ITAR is built to control; licensing it via an open API to multiple third-party integrators without a stated export-control review is a compliance gap that can freeze a defense customer's ability to adopt the tool at scale.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The API business line reads as built for the broader commercial AM software ecosystem (Ansys, Hexagon) first, with DLA/USAF added as customer logos rather than as drivers of the compliance architecture.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) additive manufacturing part candidate tool ... U.S. Air Force (USAF) materials research software

blind_spots.blind_spot: The Navy in-situ-monitoring sensor-fusion project pulls real-time data off production-floor AM machines, but nothing in the company's materials addresses how the software gets that live data out of a likely air-gapped or network-authorization-controlled shipyard/depot environment.
blind_spots.operator_reality: NAVSEA/shipyard production floors are frequently air-gapped or under strict ATO-controlled network boundaries; a tool built and demoed on exported CSV data faces a very different integration problem pulling live sensor-fusion data out of a secured production network.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The project is still active (through July 2027) and the public-facing materials describe the technical goal (consistency/verification via ML) rather than the IT integration path into the actual production network.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Senvol Leads U.S. Navy Program on AM Sensor Fusion

opener_hook: You're running Navy and Army funded AM machine-learning programs at once on a 2-person team — who inherits the reporting and sustainment load when one period of performance ends?
what_they_do: Provides a commercial additive-manufacturing data database, API, and machine-learning software (Senvol ML) for qualifying and optimizing AM machines/materials, with parallel Navy and Army-funded R&D extending the ML capability for defense in-situ monitoring.
